note: The five fact losses the v0.2.0 run produced. Each entry names the clause the rewrite dropped, in the words the judge used to rule it a loss, and the SKILL.md rubric clause that now covers it. Nothing here is re-judged: A29 asks only whether the contract we ship states the rule the judge applied.

cases.dropped_clause: the job waits in the dead-letter queue because a human has to review it
cases.kept_instead: the job is parked in the dead-letter queue
cases.judge_reason: The original states parked jobs wait for a human to review them, but the rewrite only says the job is 'parked in queue/dead' without stating that human review is the reason it's waiting there — that fact is dropped, not just compressed.

cases.dropped_clause: the cache grows because each distinct requested URL adds an entry
cases.judge_reason: The original states each distinct requested URL adds a cache entry; the rewrite only says 'entries pile up forever' without mentioning that URLs are the specific mechanism/key driving growth, dropping that detail.

cases.dropped_clause: the error shape is inconsistent, which is why client code has to branch so much
cases.kept_instead: a bullet list of the error shapes
cases.judge_reason: The rewrite drops the original's causal claim that the inconsistent error shape is why client code has to do so much branching — that consequence/reason is not retrievable from the bullet list.

cases.dropped_clause: the switch buffers so that the flow is simpler to reason about
cases.kept_instead: buffering holds the rows in memory
cases.judge_reason: The original notes buffering is 'simpler to reason about' as the tradeoff motivating the switch; the rewrite drops this characterization entirely, keeping only the memory-holding fact.

cases.dropped_clause: the dependency is pinned to an exact version, not to a version range
cases.judge_reason: The rewrite drops the specific detail that the dependency is pinned to an exact version rather than a version range, only saying 'Pin is deliberate' without that distinction.
cases.coverage_note: Not a causal link — the plan groups it with the qualifying clauses (patch1 §1). The pre-existing 'any claim the reader cannot re-derive' clause is what rules it a loss, and A29 checks that clause is still there.
